newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Sweden's Asbrink says EMU deal removes delay fears.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Asbrink says EMU deal removes delay fears.

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Monday that an earlier European Union accord on monetary union's stability pact removed all worries of a delay in the single currency project.

"There was fear for a short period of time that there would be difficulties, maybe a delay, in our work but with agreement today all these worries have been eliminated," he told reporters at a two-day summit of EU leaders in Amsterdam.
"Work is going on according to the time schedule."
Asbrink welcomed the agreement on a growth and employment resolution as well as the stability pact.
"We have both these two pillars which are of equal importance for the future cooperation in Europe," he said.
He cautioned that no-one should expect immediate or dramatic job effects but that it was important the EU was seen to be giving top priority to employment.
